question: A bullet of small mass and high velocity can penetrate a target deeper than a heavy stone thrown at the same speed because:
solution:
The correct answer is __**it is sharper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A bullet of **small mass and high velocity** penetrates a target deeper than a heavy stone thrown at the same speed mainly because the **tip of the bullet is sharp**, which helps it exert a greater pressure on the target.
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the force acting per unit area. The formula is **Pressure = Force/Area**.
 
• The sharp tip of a bullet has a **very small area of contact**. Therefore, the force produced by its motion is concentrated over a smaller area, resulting in **greater pressure** and deeper penetration.
 
• Although the bullet has a smaller mass compared to a stone, its **sharp pointed shape** allows it to overcome the resistance offered by the target material more effectively.
 
• **Hence, the sharpness of the bullet increases the pressure on the target surface, allowing it to penetrate deeper.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Effect of Sharpness on Pressure:**

 
 
• Objects with a **smaller contact area** produce more pressure when the same force is applied.
 
• Examples include a **sharp knife cutting easily**, a **needle piercing cloth**, and a **nail entering wood**.
 
• In each case, the pointed end reduces the contact area and increases the pressure.
 
 
 
• **Momentum and Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• A moving bullet possesses **kinetic energy** due to its velocity. The formula for kinetic energy is **K.E. = ½mv²**, where **m** represents mass and **v** represents velocity.
 
• A bullet travelling at a very high velocity can carry significant kinetic energy even though its mass is small.
 
• This high energy helps the bullet overcome the resistance of the target material.
 
 
 
• **Inertia and Mass:**
 
 
• **Inertia** is the tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion.
 
• The inertia of an object depends on its **mass**; a heavier object has greater inertia.
 
• However, in this case, the deeper penetration is not due to greater mass or inertia but due to the **sharp shape and high pressure** produced by the bullet.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Heavy Stone:**
 
 
• A heavy stone may have greater **mass** and therefore greater inertia, but its broad surface area distributes the force over a larger area.
 
• Due to lower pressure at the point of contact, it does not penetrate the target as effectively as a sharp bullet.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pressure:** **Force per unit area**.
 
• **Formula:** **Pressure = Force/Area**.
 
• **Smaller area of contact** results in **higher pressure**.
 
• **Bullet penetration:** Mainly depends on **sharp pointed shape, high velocity, and concentration of force over a small area**.
 
• **Correct concept:** A bullet penetrates deeper not because of greater mass or inertia, but because its **sharp tip produces high pressure on the target.**
